title_i18n.en: Let AI Truly "Understand Time": A New Breakthrough in QC-MHM Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering | AAAI
title_i18n.es: Que la IA realmente entienda el tiempo: el nuevo avance de QC-MHM en la consulta de grafos de conocimiento temporales | AAAI

excerpt_i18n.en: Consider this question: "What was the Olympic weightlifting world record before Lasha Talakhadze broke it?" Or "Who was the mayor of Budapest during the 25th Olympic Games?" Such questions are very prone to failure in Google Search or even ChatGPT. The reason is simple—they all involve time constraints, requiring the model to understand temporal words like "before" and "during," and precisely pinpoint specific entities at specific time points in a vast repository of facts.
excerpt_i18n.es: Imagina esta pregunta: "¿Cuál era el récord mundial de halterofilia olímpica antes de que Lasha Talakhadze lo batiera?" O "¿Quién era el alcalde de Budapest durante los 25º Juegos Olímpicos?" Este tipo de preguntas son muy propensas a fallar en Google e incluso en ChatGPT. La razón es simple: todas implican restricciones temporales, requiriendo que el modelo entienda términos secuenciales como "antes" o "durante", y localice con precisión una entidad específica en un punto temporal concreto dentro de un vasto corpus de hechos.

items.title: Mkrrm – a waitlist only AI can use
items.raw_excerpt:
Agents nowadays can research anything but complete nothing; practically every task ends with the model handing you a link to go click yourself. mkrrm is my attempt at fixing that
Under the hood, everything runs locally on your machine. The agent gets their own browser; separate from yours, invisible, running on your hardware, which can optionally share your browser profile, so it's signed into what you're signed into without you setting anything up. Nothing is sent to us, nothing is stored on our servers, and you never type a password anywhere new. From the agent's side, services show up as discoverable capabilities that return structured results, instead of a screen it has to screenshot and guess at.
The waitlist is a demo of the idea: there's no form. Paste "tell me all about mkrrm.com"

items.title: Build an AI-powered AWS support companion with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.raw_excerpt: In this post, you build an AWS Support Companion using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The agent uses Strands Agents as the orchestration framework and connects to AWS services through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). By the end, you have a working agent that can analyze CloudWatch logs, search AWS documentation, query community knowledge from AWS re:Post, and create support cases, all from a single conversational interface. The solution deploys with a single script using AWS CloudFormation and includes a web frontend built on AWS Amplify for interacting with the agent.
